title: A pattern compiled with flags its text cannot carry is refused at the call; one without them is accepted.
why: behavioural spec 'regex': a pattern the language represents with out-of-band options — flags, modifiers — that the pattern text cannot carry is refused at the call, before any document is built: silently dropping an option would change what the pattern means.
note: A flag belongs to a language's own pattern type (a RegExp, a java.util.regex.Pattern), which data cannot spell, so each language has a subject (ADR 0076 decision 5). How a language refuses is the style guide's business: the case checks that the call fails and that its error names the flags.
